content:
Earlier than June, we had already highlighted three examples pointing out that sanctioned Russian banks were smuggling their client applications onto the App Store. Two months later, similar cases have once again reached the top of the iPhone App Store.

K8CHEN PRO is the latest example. Its App Store product page disguises itself as an augmented reality (AR)-powered kitchen design application.

As soon as you open this app, the disguise immediately falls apart. The privacy policy linked from the App Store claims to have been generated by "Free Privacy Policy Generator," which in itself should raise a red flag.

In short, this app is definitely T-Bank's client application. What I find interesting is how these kinds of apps can repeatedly get past App Store's review process.

When they receive enough attention and climb up the App Store charts, everyone can see that these apps really shouldn't be there. The situation is truly puzzling.

The two cases from June can be seen here and here.

Update: Sure enough, this app has already been removed from the App Store.
